label: sec:archimedean-models-intro
html:
Over \mathbb{R} and \mathbb{C}, the substrate parameter q varies smoothly, and the categorical axioms take the form of differential geometry on a contact three-manifold. Every Archimedean quantum observable universe is realized as a \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})-bundle over a strictly pseudoconvex CR base equipped with an \mathrm{SU}(2) frame.

Four explicit geometric constructions illustrate the scope of the Archimedean axioms:

  • Calabi–Yau hypersurfaces: a real hypersurface in a K3 surface inherits a strictly pseudoconvex CR structure whose contact data recovers classical instanton moduli.
  • Asymptotically locally Euclidean (ALE) spaces: resolution of aKleinian quotient \mathbb{C}^2/\Gamma yields an ADE orbifold whose tautological bundles realize the McKay correspondence.
  • The unit circle bundle over Bring's surface: the Seifert fibration over the genus-four curve \Sigma_4 (\chi(\Sigma_4) = -6) produces the canonical five-fold symmetric fibre geometry.
  • Cosmological endpoints: the limiting regimes q \to 1 and q \to \infty isolate the classical symmetric limit and the deep-quantum saturation boundary.

Invariants of an Archimedean model arise from two complementary sources. The principal bundle supplies gauge-theoretic data—the instanton connection, irreducibility criteria, self-dual curvature, and the Seiberg–Witten differential—while the Reeb fibre supplies contact-geometric data through the Levi form, the Tanaka–Webster metric, and the q-deformed Heisenberg commutator. A spatial-realization functor intertwines these two descriptions and matches the categorical action against the classical Chern–Simons functional before the subsequent section transports the construction to \mathbb{Q}_p.
